name: Tarangire and Lake Manyara
tagline: Giant baobabs and huge elephant herds at Tarangire, and a soda lake with tree-climbing lions at Manyara.
highlight: Watching elephant herds feed beneath ancient baobab trees in the dry season.
shortDescription: Two compact parks on the northern circuit, famous for dry-season elephants, baobab landscapes, birdlife and the Rift Valley escarpment.
metaDescription: Tarangire and Lake Manyara travel guide: elephants and baobabs, tree-climbing lions, flamingos, walking and night safaris, lodges, costs and a two-day plan.

image.alt: An elephant herd walking across the plains in Tarangire

intro: Tarangire and Lake Manyara are the two parks usually done first on the northern safari circuit, with the quiet ease of shorter drives and fewer crowds than the Serengeti. Both are within a few hours of Arusha, making them ideal for a short trip.

Tarangire is famous for its huge elephant herds, which gather along the Tarangire River in the dry season, from June to October, when other water sources run dry. Its landscape is dotted with giant baobab trees, some over a thousand years old, and it is a good place for lions, leopards, giraffes and a long list of birds.

Lake Manyara is a small park squeezed between a Rift Valley escarpment and an alkaline lake. Groundwater forest, open floodplain and acacia woodland hold baboons, hippos, giraffes and, famously, lions that sometimes climb trees. The lake attracts thousands of flamingos in some seasons.
